title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6625 – Reuters estimate
body: Earlier, some important news: China's central bank, regulators to meet on stock support after record 12-week slide - The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks.

title: BTCPay Server tells operators to shut down after reports of hot wallets being drained
body: BTCPay Server, the open-source software many merchants use to accept Bitcoin payments without a third-party processor, has told operators to shut down their instances after receiving reports that hot wallets on multiple servers were being drained by unauthorized attackers. --- Adding to concerens re the drain last week: investingLive Asia-Pacific market news: Binance hack shakes crypto --- In a post on X, the project asked anyone running an instance to take it offline with its shutdown command until the investigation is complete. BTCPay has not yet disclosed the cause of the attack, how many servers were affected or how much was taken. A hot wallet is one whose private keys sit on an internet-connected server, so it can send funds automatically, for example to pay out refunds. That convenience makes it a bigger target than offline storage. The incident involves software built around Bitcoin, not the Bitcoin network itself. The warning follows two recent security events at the project. On October 29, BTCPay released emergency version 2.4.7 to fix one critical and several medium-risk vulnerabilities. In August, attackers exploited a separate flaw to steal Lightning Network credentials and drain nodes running behind BTCPay, including one operated by hardware wallet maker Foundation. At that time, BTCPay said its standard on-chain wallets, including hot wallets created inside the software, were not affected.

title: Market playbook: Can the RBA surprise markets again and give AUD/USD another reason to rally?
body: The aussie will be hoping that Christmas will come early this year with the RBA perhaps delivering a timely present tomorrow. But with markets already well expecting a rate hike this week, will Bullock have anything left in her bag of tricks to give the aussie another leg higher? As things stand, traders are pricing in roughly 87% odds of a 25 bps rate hike tomorrow, which will take the cash rate to 4.85%. And this will follow the rate hike from September, with inflation proving to be a rather stubborn headache to deal with for policymakers. But looking further out, traders are barely pricing in any further tightening beyond the one expected tomorrow. In fact, traders only see around 33 bps of cumulative rate hikes by June 2027 and that includes the expected move this week. Essentially, that is signaling a one more and done move by the RBA. So, could the central bank catch traders off guard given the backdrop ahead of tomorrow? I would argue that it's not outside of the realms of possibility as the central bank will want to retain as much flexibility and optionality as they can, as do all major central banks these days. The more hawkish scenario would be a 25 bps hike accompanied by stronger warnings on inflation and a clear indication that further tightening remains firmly on the table. And if Bullock explicitly pushes back against expectations of an extended pause, that could force traders to rethink the rate outlook.

That's a big miss on German retail sales with consumption activity softening across the board. Looking at the breakdown, sales at petrol stations were down 3.4%, sales of food products down 1.4%, and non-food retail trade was down 2.4% in September compared to the month before. That is hardly a convincing sign that German households are dealing well with the growing inflation pressure that is tiding over Europe especially in the second half of the year. The only bright spot is that perhaps with the new temporary fuel tax relief, running from October to December, that could prop up petrol station sales. So, we'll wait and see on that. But overall, the decline across broader categories is signaling that the health of the German consumer is not doing well. Households are definitely feeling the pinch of higher price pressures and that is showing up in their spending activity/pattern. As such, that just adds another troubling sign for the ECB as the central bank is in a tight spot to balance between flagging growth conditions and higher inflation across the euro area heading into year-end.

title: US midterms 2026: Is Trump about to lose his grip on Congress?
body: I reckon that US president Trump might be in for a rude awakening after tomorrow. Or perhaps he is already aware of his current predicament, although I wouldn't put it past him to refuse to accept that reality. Either way, he's going to have to deal with the possibility that his grip on Congress could be slipping away. As the US heads to the polls tomorrow, both the control of the House and Senate hang in the balance. And if the latest polls are anything to go by, Republicans have plenty of reasons to be nervous. The national generic congressional ballot polls show Democrats holding a sizeable lead over Republicans as cost-of-living frustrations and dissatisfaction with Trump's presidency have weighed on sentiment. Having said that, the national polling doesn't necessarily translate neatly into congressional seats. So, what does this mean for markets? Let's start with a bit of backdrop. Democrats need a net gain of three seats in the House and four in the Senate to wrest control of both chambers from Republicans. If Republicans lose the House, then Trump's legislative agenda could essentially run into a brick wall. As for Democrats, that would open the door to more investigations and tougher negotiations over government spending, taxation and funding. But what if Democrats take both chambers? Well, that would certainly tighten the screws further especially when it comes to Trump's judicial appointments and other nominations requiring Senate confirmation.

The shift also changes what traders will watch: the overnight rate, not the seven-day rate, now looks set to become the signal of PBOC intent, so any future adjustment to the 1.25% level will be read as a policy move. With October PMIs in contraction and equities coming off their worst month in more than a decade, a cleaner transmission channel gives Beijing a sharper tool if it decides to lower borrowing costs. For the yuan, the change is structural rather than directional, but it modernises a framework global investors have long found opaque. --- China is quietly swapping out the dial it uses to steer interest rates, trading a seven-day benchmark for an overnight one that brings its monetary toolkit closer to the Fed's than ever before.
